text.p: Grain and oilseed exports reported by USDA and private export sources.

RICE SALE - Jordan bought 15,000 tonnes of California medium-grain rice, camolino type (oil-coated), on Tuesday for April shipment, several U.S. exporters said. The rice was purchased at $407.00 a tonne, free on truck, one exporter said.

WHEAT SALE - Syria's general establishment for cereal processing and trade has sold Algeria 150,000 tonnes of hard amber durum wheat for delivery in April/May, a GECPT official said. The exact price was not disclosed.

SOYOIL SALE - U.S. exporters said China bought 4,000 to 5,000 tonnes of Brazilian soybean oil Monday for June shipment. One exporter said China paid $508 per tonne, FOB, for 3,000 tonnes and $505 for 2,000 tonnes, all for June shipment. Another said the deal was for 4,000 tonnes at $505 per tonne for June shipment.

WHEAT TENDER - Algeria has relaunched a previously postponed import tender for 75,000 tonnes of April/May wheat, grain traders said. The tender was originally in the market last week but was postponed on Friday.

WHEAT TENDERS - South Korea invited tenders to buy 21,500 tonnes of U.S. No.1 wheat by 2.00 p.m. (0500 GMT) on Wednesday, traders said. Shipment was set for May 5-June 5 to the western port of Inchon.

- South Korea's Daehan Flour Mills Co Ltd invited tenders to buy 24,000 tonnes of U.S. No.1 wheat by 2:00 p.m. (0500 GMT) on Wednesday, traders said. Shipment was set for May 15-June 15 to the western port of Inchon.
- The Philippines rejected an offer of 23,500 tonnes of U.S. wheat. The mill had sought 16,000 tonnes of U.S. dark northern spring wheat and 7,500 tonnes of western white wheat.
WHEAT TENDER - Iraq is still negotiating the import of 50,000 tonnes of U.S. hard red winter wheat and a reply is expected later on Monday or on Tuesday, European traders said.
- France will hold a tender on March 26 to sell 3,000 tonnes of soft wheat to Iraq via the Rome-based World Food Programme, national grain office ONIC said. The wheat is for shipment April 8-30.
WHEAT TENDER - Cyprus changed the deadline for the submission of tenders for 10,000 tonnes of spring and 8,000 tonnes of durum wheat to March 27. The commission had said the deadline was March 28.
VEGOIL TENDER - Egypt was seeking up to 45,000 tonnes of assorted vegetable oils for delivery in May 1997. The deadline for all bids was April 2.
BARLEY TENDER - The South African Wheat Board said it was offering 25,150 tonnes of feed grade barley for export sale no later than April 30.
RICE TENDERS - Syria seeks 12,000 tonnes of white rice for shipment between April 20 and May 20. April 8 is the final date for bids and result will be announced on April 16.

MARKET TALK - Malaysia and Indonesia were said to have bought small cargoes of Chinese corn, but regional business was quiet and the impact of the Taiwan pork crisis appears to be dying down, regional traders said. "We heard that the Malaysians bought about 10,000 to 15,000 tonnes of Chinese corn for May shipment. I understand the price was around US$149 or $150 (a tonne C&F)," a trader for a U.S. commodity trading house said.
... The Thai grains and oilseed market attracted brisk enquiry for corn this week after the cabinet approved a zero-tariff corn import quota of 200,000 tonnes for 1997, trade sources said on Tuesday.
Although the industry was still awaiting official allocation of the quota, most feed mills looked set to order if the right prices could be found, they said.
One major feed producer told Reuters he was seeking 50,000 tonnes of corn for April/May shipment, very likely from Argentina.
